directAnswer: An environment variable is a dynamic value that can affect the way running processes will behave on a computer. They are often used to store configuration settings and system paths.
summary: Environment variables are key-value pairs that provide information about the environment in which a process runs, allowing for flexible configuration of applications.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: Environment variables are part of the environment in which a process runs. They can include system paths, user preferences, and other configuration settings that can be accessed by applications.

sections.heading: Usage
sections.body: Developers use environment variables to manage application settings without hardcoding values. This practice enhances security and flexibility, especially in different environments like development, testing, and production.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Variables
sections.body: Different operating systems have their own sets of environment variables. For example, on Windows, variables like %PATH% are commonly used, while on Unix-based systems, variables such as $HOME are prevalent.

steps.title: Viewing Environment Variables on Windows
steps.detail: Open Command Prompt and type 'set' to display all environment variables.

steps.title: Viewing Environment Variables on macOS/Linux
steps.detail: Open Terminal and type 'printenv' to list all environment variables.

steps.title: Setting an Environment Variable on Windows
steps.detail: Use the command 'set VAR_NAME=value' in Command Prompt to create or modify an environment variable for the session.

steps.title: Setting an Environment Variable on macOS/Linux
steps.detail: Use the command 'export VAR_NAME=value' in Terminal to create or modify an environment variable for the session.

faqs.question: How do I make an environment variable permanent?
faqs.answer: On Windows, you can set environment variables permanently through System Properties > Environment Variables. On macOS/Linux, add the export command to your shell's configuration file (e.g., .bashrc or .zshrc).

faqs.question: Can environment variables be accessed by all applications?
faqs.answer: Environment variables set in a terminal session are only accessible to processes spawned from that session. To make them globally accessible, set them in the system settings.

faqs.question: What is the difference between user and system environment variables?
faqs.answer: User environment variables are specific to a user account, while system environment variables apply to all users on the system.

caveats: Environment variables can be overwritten by other processes or scripts, which may lead to unexpected behavior.
